insight: For Tunisia, hydration breaks in the 2026 World Cup have generally been a positive turning point, with the team gaining momentum in 4 out of 6 breaks, resulting in a slight increase in performance. This is evident in the average change in momentum of +0.067 per minute after a break, indicating that the team tends to come back stronger. However, when Tunisia was pressing before a break, they struggled to maintain their momentum, with a significant decrease in performance, whereas when they weren't pressing, they were able to capitalize on the break and boost their performance, with an average increase of +0.120 per minute. Overall, these statistics suggest that hydration breaks have been a crucial factor in Tunisia's matches, allowing them to regroup and refocus, particularly when they're not under intense pressure.
